title: Interferometric Signatures of Zero Modes in Fractional Quantum Hall-Superconductor Heterostructures
authors: Junyi Cao, Ramanjit Sohal, Angela Kou, Eduardo Fradkin
abstract: Fractional quantum Hall-superconductor (FQH-SC) heterostructures are predicted to host defect-bound parafermion zero modes (PZMs). We propose two related configurations to probe their fusion structure. In a Josephson junction coupled to a single quantum point contact (QPC), quasiparticle tunneling switches the defect fusion channel, producing stochastic transitions between branches of the fractional Josephson spectrum. Embedding the junction in a two-QPC Fabry-Pérot interferometer provides a complementary probe. Weak zero mode tunneling produces fusion-channel-dependent interference while strong tunneling makes the interferometer probe a superposition of fusion channels and strongly suppresses the signal: in the topological limit it vanishes exactly, revealing the defects' non-Abelian nature even when the parent FQH state is Abelian.
summary: This theoretical work develops a method to probe the exotic fusion structure of parafermion zero modes in FQH-SC heterostructures using superconducting interferometers. By analyzing the interference signal in the two-QPC setup, the authors predict that strong zero mode tunneling causes the interference term to vanish exactly. This cancellation serves as a unique, measurable signature confirming the non-Abelian nature of the underlying topological order.
main_problem: The paper investigates how interferometric measurements can probe the fusion structure of defect-bound parafermion zero modes (PZMs) in Fractional Quantum Hall-Superconductor (FQH-SC) heterostructures.
main_result: Strong zero mode tunneling leads to the exact cancellation of the interference signal in the Fabry-Pérot interferometer, providing a robust signature of the defects' non-Abelian nature, even when the parent FQH state is Abelian.
method: The analysis uses theoretical calculations involving modular S-matrices and the F-move to evaluate the expectation value of loop operators, comparing different fusion bases.
model_or_system: The system is FQH-SC heterostructures, modeled using anyon statistics, Josephson junctions, and Quantum Point Contacts (QPCs). The physics is analyzed for Laughlin and Moore-Read states.
key_observables: Interference conductance ($\sigma_{xx}$), fractional Josephson spectrum periodicity, and the expectation value of the loop operator ($\langle W_{Nqh,b} angle$).
important_parameters: Tunneling amplitudes ($\lambda_a$, $\Gamma$), superconducting phase difference ($\phi_{SC}$), and the topological limit.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on treating zero mode tunneling perturbatively and assumes specific fixed total fusion channels for the defects.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the two proposed device configurations: a single-QPC junction and a two-QPC Fabry-Pérot interferometer. Figure 2 shows QPC-induced fusion-channel shifts in Laughlin and MR systems.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the physics in two main setups (single-QPC vs. two-QPC interferometer), deriving spectral properties for Abelian and non-Abelian cases, and culminating in the calculation of the interference term based on the F-move algebra.
why_interesting: The mechanism of interference cancellation due to non-Abelian statistics is a powerful diagnostic tool, providing a clean signature of topological order that can be measured using superconducting circuits, which is relevant for understanding emergent quantum phenomena in condensed matter.
